sections.h2: How do I sell an inherited house in Lauderhill?
sections.html:
Start by finding out who has legal authority to sign the deed. If the owner died with the house in their sole name, a personal representative usually needs court appointment before a buyer's title company will close.

Florida offers shortcuts for smaller estates. Summary administration is open when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or when the owner has been dead more than two years (s. 735.201). Where only exempt property and a small amount of other personal property remain, the court may allow a transfer on informal application (s. 735.301). A house is real property, so most Lauderhill inheritances still go through some form of administration in Broward County court.

Creditors matter to timing. A claim is barred unless filed by the later of three months after the first publication of the notice to creditors or 30 days after service on a creditor who had to be served (s. 733.702). Heirs who sell before that window closes should expect the title company to hold funds or require estate documents.

  • Gather the death certificate, will if any, and the deed.
  • Ask the Broward clerk what the probate division needs for a house.
  • Keep paying taxes and insurance while the estate is open.

sections.h2: Is there a Florida estate tax on a Lauderhill inheritance?
sections.html:
No. The state's estate tax ended for anyone who died after December 31, 2004, and the Department of Revenue says personal representatives have not needed to file Form DR-312 or DR-313 since July 1, 2023.

Deed tax is separate. The Department says a personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxable for documentary stamps, yet it also states that no specific exemption exists for transfers made for estate planning purposes. If heirs instead sell, the buyer's deed carries the normal rate of 70 cents per $100 of consideration.

sections.h2: What happens to the homestead exemption and tax cap when the owner dies or sells?
sections.html:
Both change. Homestead covers an owner's permanent residence as of January 1, and the exemption is lost once the home is rented, stops being the permanent home, or the owner is no longer a Florida resident.

The Save Our Homes limit holds the annual rise in assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, and the Department's chart shows a 2.7 percent cap for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024. A sale or other change of title resets the property to just value the next January 1, with exceptions for spouse transfers and certain transfers at death (s. 193.155). Heirs who plan to keep and rent the house should expect a higher assessment than the decedent paid.

A homeowner selling to buy another Florida homestead may move part of the capped benefit. The new homestead must be established within three years of January 1 of the year the old one was abandoned, and Form DR-501T goes in with the DR-501 by March 1.

sections.h2: What tax dates should a Lauderhill seller watch?
sections.html:
The Broward County Property Appraiser values the house and approves exemptions, while the Broward tax collector bills and collects. These dates come from the Department of Revenue's calendar for property owners.

Property tax steps for a Broward County home
StepTimingOffice
File for exemptionsBy March 1Property appraiser
Proposed tax notice (TRIM)AugustProperty appraiser
Challenge a valueWithin 25 days of the noticeClerk of the court
Tax billsNovemberTax collector
DelinquencyApril 1Tax collector

The appraiser's office lists 954-357-6830 and weekday hours of 8 am to 5 pm. Heirs who inherit a house with an unpaid bill should ask the tax collector what is owed, because tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1.

sections.h2: What does Lauderhill's city government offer sellers?
sections.html:
The City of Lauderhill describes itself as a municipality in the southeastern part of Florida in Broward County, and its site carries notices, meetings and news. In November 2026 it listed a neighborhood district meeting for the Isles of Inverrary and announced a new police chief sworn in at City Hall.

Neighborhood-level meetings are a useful read before listing, because they show which blocks are active and what the city is discussing. For permits on repairs, code questions or a certificate of occupancy, call the city directly before you commit to a price. Any unpermitted work you disclose or a buyer discovers can slow a closing.

  • Ask the city whether open permits or code cases exist on the address.
  • Have the title company search for municipal liens.
  • Keep receipts for any repair you do before selling.

sections.h2: Which Lauderhill sale route fits an estate or tired house?
sections.html:
A cash purchase tends to fit a house the heirs do not want to repair, with belongings inside and out-of-state family. A listing may bring a higher price if the house is clean and the estate has a few months.

Compare an agent's net after commission and repairs to a straight cash number, and put both on paper. Ask each buyer who pays the stamp tax and recording charges, and whether the buyer will close on the estate's timetable once the personal representative has authority.

sections.h2: Which deed types come up when heirs or relatives transfer a Lauderhill house?
sections.html:
Four deed types turn up most: warranty, special warranty, quit claim and personal representative's deed. State revenue guidance treats the first three as taxable, as it does life estate deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure.

A quitclaim between relatives is not a way around the cost. It is taxable if consideration is involved, and it counts as a change of ownership for Save Our Homes unless an exception applies, such as a transfer between spouses. A lady bird deed is different: a 2020 Department of Revenue advisement concluded that a deed of that kind, on the facts given, passed no present beneficial interest and so owed no stamp tax. Have a Florida attorney check whether your facts match before you rely on it.

Florida requires a conveyance of land to be in writing and signed with two subscribing witnesses (s. 689.01), and recording fees under s. 28.24 start at $5.00 for page one.

sections.h2: How should heirs compare offers on a Lauderhill house?
sections.html:
Put every offer on one sheet with the same lines: price, repairs the buyer expects you to make, who pays the deed tax, who pays recording, and the closing date. An offer that looks high can lose that lead once those lines are filled in.

Ask whether the buyer closes with no financing contingency, whether a deposit becomes non-refundable, and what happens if the estate needs extra weeks for court paperwork. Written answers to those four questions protect every heir who signs.

faqs.q: Can an heir sell a Lauderhill house before probate finishes?
faqs.a: Usually not until a personal representative has authority to convey. Smaller estates can use summary administration, which applies at $150,000 or less in non-exempt assets or two years after death (s. 735.201). Ask a probate attorney or the Broward clerk which track applies.

faqs.q: Does Florida charge estate tax on a house passed to heirs?
faqs.a: No. Florida has had no estate tax for deaths after December 31, 2004, and personal representatives have not needed Form DR-312 or DR-313 since July 1, 2023.

faqs.q: What is the Save Our Homes cap in 2026?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue's chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026 (CPI 2.7 percent). The cap is the lower of 3 percent or CPI. It resets after a sale or other change of ownership.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax when a Lauderhill house sells?
faqs.a: The signers share liability whichever party the contract names, at 70 cents per $100 of consideration in Broward (s. 201.02).

faqs.q: How long do creditors have to file claims against an estate?
faqs.a: The later of three months after the first publication of the notice to creditors or 30 days after service on a creditor who must be served (s. 733.702). Late claims are barred, with exceptions in the statute.
